claim: Flat-rate 'unlimited' AI SaaS plans frequently conceal usage caps that only become visible after purchase, e.g., Otter.ai's Pro plan caps at 1,200 transcription minutes/month with a 90-minute per-conversation limit despite its flat-rate framing.
stance_target: general principle that nominal pricing hides true usage-based cost, applicable to agent subscription economics (Pillar 6)
quoted_support: Otter.ai's Pro plan costs $8.33/user/month billed annually but caps users at 1,200 transcription minutes per month with a 90-minute per-conversation limit.

claim: Enterprise AI SaaS vendors like Gong add mandatory platform fees of $5,000-$50,000 annually plus a separate professional-services onboarding fee on top of per-seat pricing, in addition to a per-user rate around $250/month.
stance_target: hidden enterprise AI tooling costs relevant to total-cost-of-ownership modeling (Pillar 6)
quoted_support: At the enterprise end, Gong's pricing adds a mandatory platform fee on top of per-seat costs, with buyers reporting fees from $5,000 to $50,000 annually, approximately $250/user/month for the standard package, and a $7,500 professional services onboarding fee.
